question: True or false: a fluorescent orange paint can send back more orange light than the orange light falling on it?
answer: True. An ordinary pigment can only return part of each colour it receives. A fluorescent one also absorbs blue and ultraviolet and re-emits that energy as orange, so at orange wavelengths its measured reflectance can pass 100%. That extra glow, made from light the eye barely registers, is why safety vests seem lit from within.
move: Check whether the output was converted from something you were not counting.
trap: False, because no surface returns more light than it receives.
reference: Christie, Colour Chemistry, 2nd edition, Royal Society of Chemistry, 2015
